---
title: "The probable relation typo that warns but never autocorrects"
---

REQ-A intends to use the catalog relation `verified-by`, but the authored key
is `verifed-by` — one deletion away. Quarto-Needs reports `QND005` as a
warning because the key is a conservative one-edit near miss of a real
relation name.

The advisory never repairs the source and never invents an edge. The original
`verifed-by` key remains an ordinary attribute until the author explicitly
changes it to `verified-by`. This preserves the open custom-attribute
namespace while surfacing the most likely accidental relation misspellings.

::: {.need #REQ-A type="functional-requirement" status="draft" verifed-by="TC-B"}
## Signed payloads

The service shall sign every payload it emits.

### Rationale

The author intended TC-B to verify this requirement, but the misspelled key
must not silently become a graph relation.
:::

::: {.need #TC-B type="test-case" status="draft"}
## Payload signature verification

A draft verification case that would be the relation target after the author
corrects `verifed-by` to `verified-by`.
:::
